stories.head: Blinkit delivers GTA 6 in 11 cities at ₹5,999, the same price as the PlayStation Store, as the game finally launches
stories.dek: Eternal's quick-commerce app began dropping boxed PS5 download codes for GTA 6 a day before the global release. 'It took 13 years,' says CEO Albinder Dhindsa.

sections.title: What's on offer
paras: Blinkit has started delivering Grand Theft Auto VI for the PlayStation 5 in parts of 11 cities: Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad, Noida, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, Kolkata and Ahmedabad. More cities were due to be added on 18 and 19 November.

Buyers don't get a disc. The box holds a digital code that is redeemed on the PlayStation Store, and the game unlocks in India at midnight. The Standard Edition costs ₹5,999, the same as Sony's own store. The listing is for PS5 only, even though the game is also out on Xbox Series X|S.

sections.title: Why it's a smart brand move
paras: Blinkit CEO Albinder Dhindsa announced the drop himself, joking that 'it took 13 years for GTA 6 to be released'. For a quick-commerce app, being the place where gamers get the year's biggest launch in minutes is cheap, viral marketing.

It fits a pattern. Blinkit has tried a 10-minute ambulance service in Gurugram, printouts and passport photos, and a 'Scream for Ice Cream' discount stunt. Rivals Zepto, Swiggy Instamart, Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now and BigBasket are all fighting for the same impulse orders.

sections.title: The business behind the buzz
paras: In the July–September quarter, Blinkit's net order value rose 79.3% to ₹20,940 crore and revenue grew 93.6% to ₹19,152 crore. It made an adjusted EBITDA profit of ₹184 crore, compared with a ₹156 crore loss a year earlier.
It added 308 dark stores in the quarter, taking the total to 2,751, and plans more than 3,500 by March 2027 and about 5,000 by March 2028.

facts: Blinkit Q2 FY27 net order value: ₹20,940 crore, up 79.3%

stories.head: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share, above its range, raising $81.3 billion; trading on Nasdaq as 'ANT' starts today
stories.dek: The Claude maker sold about 980 million shares, more than planned, valuing it at roughly $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

sections.title: The deal
paras: Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 a share on 18 November, above the $70–78 range it had marketed. It sold about 980 million Class A shares, up from a planned 825 million, raising $81.3 billion. Shares are due to start trading on Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker 'ANT', and the offering is expected to close on 20 November.

That is more than the $75 billion SpaceX raised in its base IPO deal in June (SpaceX reached $85.7 billion after extra shares were sold to underwriters). Google, Microsoft, Nvidia and AMD together agreed to buy $26 billion of stock at the IPO price.

sections.title: The numbers in the filing
paras: Revenue for the nine months to 30 September was $33.24 billion, up about 1,200% from a year earlier. Its run-rate revenue was about $81 billion at the end of October, up $10 billion in a month, CNBC reported.
The company also reported a $104 billion net loss for those nine months, mostly from changes in the value of convertible notes and derivatives rather than day-to-day operations.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: At about $1.5 trillion, Anthropic joins the world's most valuable listed companies on day one. Its seven co-founders are selling about $1.96 billion of shares between them.

How the stock trades today will be read as a test of investor appetite for AI, after a year of huge spending on chips and data centres. (Disclosure: Anthropic makes Claude, the AI model that helps produce this site.)

stories.head: Boba Bhai raises $18 million to grow from 120 to as many as 300 outlets; its revenue jumped 145% to about ₹70 crore in FY26
stories.dek: The bubble tea chain, founded in 2023, plans to open in Kolkata, Ahmedabad and Chandigarh within three to six months.
stat: Series B led by Left Lane Capital

sections.title: The round
paras: Boba Bhai has raised $18 million (about ₹168 crore) in a Series B round led by US-based Left Lane Capital, with BIG Capital and existing backer Titan Capital joining. Most of it is fresh money, with a small part going to earlier investors. Its Series A, about ₹40 crore, came only in March.

sections.title: How big it is
paras: Founded by Dhruv Kohli in 2023, Boba Bhai runs 120 outlets and serves about 3.5 lakh orders a month. Bengaluru is its biggest market, with Mumbai and Karnal also doing well, and it is in cities like Lucknow, Jaipur and Kanpur.

Net revenue rose 145% to about ₹70 crore in FY26 from ₹28 crore, while the loss widened 32% to ₹12.5 crore. The company says it already beat its full-year FY26 revenue in the first half of FY27 and now makes about ₹12.5 crore a month.

sections.title: What's next
paras: The plan is 250–300 outlets in the next 12 months and 1,000 in the long run, with Kolkata, Ahmedabad and Chandigarh next. It is testing a second brand, Oreco Mexican Kitchen, in Bengaluru, and selling Korean chips on Blinkit in five cities.
Quick commerce already brings about 1,500 orders a day, and online orders make up about 60% of revenue.

stories.head: The 'Dhoni discount': CSK's sponsorship value could fall 10–15% after his IPL exit, say marketers, as 17 brands post farewell tributes
stories.dek: From Zomato to Netflix, brands lined up to say goodbye to MS Dhoni, while ad experts debate what Chennai Super Kings loses without him on the field.
stat: possible hit to CSK's sponsorship value

sections.title: What marketers expect
paras: Parle Products CMO Mayank Shah told Storyboard18 he expects CSK's brand valuation to drop 10–15% after Dhoni's retirement as a player, with viewership of CSK matches falling by less than 10%. A former FMCG marketer said sponsorship rate cards could also dip 10–15%.
Not everyone agrees. Baseline Ventures' Ramakrishnan Ram does not expect a big hit, pointing to a gradual handover with Ruturaj Gaikwad as captain and Dhoni staying on as Team Mentor.

sections.title: What's at stake
paras: CSK earned ₹116.35 crore from sponsorships in FY2024-25, up 7.2% from ₹108.52 crore, and had 21 brand partners in the 2025 season, including Etihad Airways, FedEx and Gulf Oil. A 2026 Houlihan Lokey study valued the CSK brand at $244 million; Kroll valued Dhoni's personal brand at $115.3 million in 2025.
The IPL 2027 mini-auction is on 16 December.

sections.title: The tribute wave
paras: Social Samosa counted 17 brands posting farewells. Zomato asked 'why does goodbye have 7 letters', Netflix India called him 'GOAT for a reason', Prime Video said 'game recognises game' and JioSaavn said no song makes this goodbye easier. Swiggy, Flipkart, Domino's, KitKat and BookMyShow also joined in.

stories.head: Cyclone Akvan turns very severe ahead of Friday's landfall; Odisha moves about 50,000 people and Andhra puts 7 districts on red alert
stories.dek: The storm's track has shifted north, and landfall is now expected between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha around noon on 20 November.
stat: people moved to safety in Odisha

sections.title: Where it's heading
paras: The India Meteorological Department expects Akvan to become a very severe cyclonic storm by Thursday evening, with winds of up to 145 km/h as it nears the coast. Landfall is likely around noon on Friday, 20 November, between Narsapur and Puri.
Red and orange alerts cover parts of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Tamil Nadu, with heavy to very heavy rain expected along coastal Andhra.

sections.title: Getting ready
paras: Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said nearly 50,000 people have been moved to safety, most of them from Ganjam district, and that the target is zero deaths. Schools are shut in six districts, employee leave has been cancelled, and about 55 landslide-prone villages in hilly Rayagada have been marked for evacuation.

In Andhra Pradesh, a red alert for extremely heavy rain covers Kakinada, East Godavari, Konaseema, Eluru, West Godavari, Krishna and Bapatla. Officials have been told to stay on high alert for the next 48 hours.

sections.title: What to do
paras: If you live in or are travelling to coastal Andhra or south Odisha, follow IMD and state disaster-management updates, avoid the sea, and keep phones charged and documents in a waterproof bag.

facts: Landfall expected around noon, Friday 20 November
Winds of up to 145 km/h expected

stories.head: GTA 6 is finally out on PS5 and Xbox after a 13-year wait; pre-orders topped $1 billion, Sensor Tower estimates
stories.dek: Rockstar's game went live at midnight local time around the world, starting in New Zealand. It is not on PC yet.

sections.title: It's here
paras: Grand Theft Auto VI went on sale at midnight local time on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, rolling out country by country from New Zealand. In India it unlocked at midnight, with the Standard Edition priced at ₹5,999. There is no PC version at launch.
The game returns to Vice City, the series' take on Miami, 13 years after GTA V.

sections.title: How big a launch
paras: App and game tracker Sensor Tower estimates pre-orders passed $1 billion and about 10.3 million copies after returns, with PlayStation making up about 75% of sales. These are estimates; Rockstar's owner Take-Two has not shared figures, though its CEO called pre-orders 'unprecedented' in August.
For comparison, Guinness World Records lists GTA V's launch-day sales at $815.7 million in 2013.

facts: Out on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S; no PC yet

stories.head: Coal India's Mahanadi Coalfields opens its ₹8,981 crore IPO today at ₹129–136 a share; one lot costs ₹14,960
stories.dek: It is a pure offer for sale: Coal India is selling about 10% of MCL, so the company itself gets no money. Crystal Crop's ₹455 crore IPO also closes on Friday.

sections.title: MCL at a glance
paras: Mahanadi Coalfields, a Coal India subsidiary, is open for bids from 19 to 23 November. The price band is ₹129–136 and retail investors must apply for at least 110 shares, or ₹14,960 at the top of the band.
The entire issue is an offer for sale, with Coal India selling up to 66.18 crore shares. Allotment is likely on 25 November and listing on BSE and NSE on 27 November.

sections.title: Also open: Crystal Crop
paras: Agrochemicals maker Crystal Crop Protection's ₹455 crore IPO, priced at ₹259–272, closes on 20 November. It was subscribed about 1.36 times by the end of day 1, with institutional buyers bidding 2.07 times their quota, according to Groww data. Listing is expected on 26 November.
As always, read the offer documents and don't invest based on grey-market chatter.

stories.head: Value fashion chain Style Union raises ₹485 crore to take on Zudio and Trends beyond south India
stories.dek: Founded in 2022 by Ekta Biyani, the brand has grown from 41 stores and ₹123 crore revenue to 200 stores and over ₹1,150 crore.

sections.title: The money
paras: Nexon Omniverse, which runs Style Union, has raised ₹485 crore (about $52 million) in a Series E round led by Venturi Partners and co-led by Elev8 Venture Partners. Investors include Ashish Kacholia, Manish Chokhani and Metro Brands' Rafique Malik. The round mixes new money and share sales by earlier backers.

sections.title: Fast growth
paras: Revenue rose from ₹123 crore in FY23 to more than ₹1,150 crore in FY26, and stores went from 41 to 158 in that time; it now runs 200 across south India, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Delhi-NCR. Gross margin has held at about 47%, while store-level EBITDA margin improved from 10% to 16%.
The new money will fund more stores in big metros in western and northern India, where it will go up against Tata's Zudio and Westside and Reliance's Trends and Yousta.

stories.head: Policybazaar co-founder Alok Bansal will step down as PB Fintech's executive vice-chairman after 18 years
stories.dek: He will stay on the board as a non-executive director from April 2027. CEO Yashish Dahiya says Bansal first wanted to step back five years ago.

sections.title: What's changing
paras: Alok Bansal, who co-founded Policybazaar with Yashish Dahiya in 2008, will leave his role as executive vice-chairman and whole-time director when his term ends on 31 March 2027. From 1 April 2027 he will be a non-executive director, if shareholders approve. He cited a 'personal desire' to step back from executive work.
Bansal, an IIM Calcutta alumnus who worked at Voltas, GE and Mahindra & Mahindra, led strategy, fundraising and investor relations, including the 2021 stock market listing.

sections.title: Part of a trend
paras: PB Fintech made a ₹192.4 crore profit on ₹2,177.7 crore of revenue in the July–September quarter. Inc42 notes a run of co-founder exits from executive roles this year, including Unacademy's Gaurav Munjal stepping down as CEO in November and BigBasket's Hari Menon and Vipul Parekh in June.

stories.head: Trump, Xi and Putin meet in Shenzhen today for their first three-way talks, with nuclear arms and the Iran war on the agenda
stories.dek: Xi broke with protocol to greet Trump on the tarmac at the APEC summit. Few expect a concrete deal.

sections.title: The setup
paras: US President Donald Trump landed in Shenzhen on Wednesday for the APEC summit and was met on the tarmac by Chinese President Xi Jinping, a rare gesture. The three-way meeting with Russia's Vladimir Putin is set for Thursday, with separate Trump–Xi talks expected to focus on trade.
Nuclear arms control and the Iran war are expected to top the agenda. Putin said he sees considerable potential benefits, while US officials have said they don't expect a deal.

sections.title: Who's watching
paras: Ukraine has asked that no decisions about it be made without its participation. Trump has said that talking to both leaders at once is an advantage because they work so closely together.

facts: Held on the sidelines of APEC in Shenzhen
Agenda: nuclear arms, Iran war, trade

stories.head: Iran fires drones at a US air base in Kuwait, its first attack on Kuwait since September, after a US strike on Qeshm Island
stories.dek: Kuwait says its air defences stopped the drones and calls the attacks 'criminal'. Qatar is holding fresh talks with Iran.

sections.title: What happened
paras: Iran's army said it targeted Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait, which hosts US forces, with drones early on 18 November. Kuwait's army said it intercepted the attack and did not report damage. Iran also fired at targets in Bahrain.
The attack came after US jets struck an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday evening, which the US said was a response to attacks on its personnel.

sections.title: Diplomacy and oil
paras: Qatari and Iranian officials met on Tuesday for talks aimed at 'narrowing the gap' between proposals, Qatar's spokesman Majed al-Ansari said. Kuwait's foreign ministry condemned the repeated attacks.
Oil markets have stayed fairly calm: Brent crude traded in the low $90s a barrel this week, well below its 30 October peak of about $117.

facts: Target: Ali Al Salem Air Base, Kuwait
Followed a US strike on Qeshm Island

stories.head: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon at $3 per million input tokens, its fourth new Gemini model in a month
stories.dek: Neon is live for paid AI Pro and Ultra subscribers and on the API, priced at twice the cheaper Gemini 4 Hydrogen.

sections.title: What's new
paras: Google released Gemini 4 Neon on 18 November. Developers pay $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, falling to $0.15 per million for cached input. There is no free API tier. In the Gemini app, it is available to AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.
It is the fourth Gemini model in about a month, and costs twice as much as Gemini 4 Hydrogen ($1.50/$7.50).

sections.title: The fine print
paras: Google says Neon brings 'Carbon quality at Flash speeds' and claims a lower cost per task than Carbon. Independent testing data is mixed so far, so the real-world value will depend on the job.

facts: Available to AI Pro and Ultra users

stories.head: Egg brand Henfruit raises $15 million, its first outside money in 12 years, and aims for ₹350 crore revenue this year
stories.dek: The bootstrapped brand processes over 4 crore eggs a month and publishes its daily lab test reports.

sections.title: The round
paras: Henfruit, founded in 2014 by Tarun Gupta, has raised $15 million in a Series A led by Lok Capital, DSG Consumer Partners and RPSG Capital Ventures. It had never taken outside funding before.
The money will go into expanding across India, more production and a bigger supply chain, online and offline.

sections.title: The business
paras: Henfruit sells in 15 cities, has more than 300 employees and expects revenue to cross ₹350 crore in FY27, after growing about 10 times in three years. Its range includes Protein Max, Farm White and Power Brown eggs, and it tests every day for antibiotics, banned drugs and freshness.
Rival Eggoz has raised over $32 million.

stories.head: Bumrah strikes on the third ball of his comeback Test as India reduce New Zealand to 95 for 5 in Wellington
stories.dek: India chose to bowl first at the Basin Reserve, and debutant Anshul Kamboj also struck early.
stat: New Zealand in the second session, day 1

sections.title: Day 1 so far
paras: Shubman Gill won the toss and bowled first. Jasprit Bumrah, playing his first Test in nearly a year after injury, removed captain Tom Latham with the third ball of the series. New Zealand slumped to 60 for 4 at lunch, with Bumrah on 2 for 17 and debutant Anshul Kamboj and Akash Deep also among the wickets.
Henry Nicholls held one end together, reaching the high 40s as New Zealand moved to 95 for 5 after 34 overs in the second session.

sections.title: What's next
paras: This is the first of two Tests. The second starts at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on 27 November. India left out Mohammed Siraj and Ravindra Jadeja for this match.

stories.head: CoinDCX says a breach at its notifications vendor exposed some users' names, emails and bank names; it says funds are safe
stories.dek: The crypto exchange blamed two incidents in October at Plotline, the company that sends its in-app messages.
stat: incidents in October at the vendor

sections.title: What leaked
paras: CoinDCX told users that unauthorised access at Plotline, its vendor for in-app messages and notifications, exposed data of a 'small number' of users between 24–26 October and 30–31 October. The data included names, email IDs and the names of banks linked to their accounts.

It did not say how many users were hit or whether the data was copied. CoinDCX says Plotline had no access to its databases, trading systems or wallets, and that customer funds are 'entirely secure and untouched'.

sections.title: What to do
paras: Affected users have been told by email. If you use CoinDCX, watch out for phishing emails or calls that mention your bank name, and never share OTPs or passwords. CoinDCX says it is tightening checks on outside vendors.

facts: Funds and wallets not affected, says CoinDCX

stories.head: DeepMind spin-off Isomorphic Labs raises $5 billion to design drugs with AI; vision-implant maker Science Corp raises $400 million
stories.dek: Investors put more than $6.6 billion into nine startups on Wednesday, led by two big bets on AI and health.

sections.title: Isomorphic Labs
paras: London-based Isomorphic Labs, spun out of Google DeepMind, raised $5 billion in a round co-led by Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, with Andreessen Horowitz, Alphabet, Thrive Capital, GV, Temasek and the UK Sovereign AI Fund also investing. It did not share its valuation.
It builds an AI system that proposes and refines drug molecules before lab work, and partners with Eli Lilly, Novartis and Johnson & Johnson. This comes on top of a $2.1 billion round in May.

sections.title: Science Corporation
paras: Science Corp raised $400 million in a Series D, reportedly at a $3.5 billion valuation. Its PRIMA system, a retinal implant with special glasses, helps some people with late-stage retinal disease see shapes again. It is sold in Europe and is seeking US approval.

facts: Science Corp raised over $900 million since 2021
$6.6 billion+ raised by 9 startups on 18 Nov

stories.head: Modi proposes free e-visas for tourists from ASEAN countries, one of nine ideas he put forward at the India–ASEAN summit in Manila
stories.dek: Travellers would still apply online, but the fee would be waived. No start date has been announced.

sections.title: The proposal
paras: At the 23rd ASEAN–India Summit in Manila on 17 November, PM Narendra Modi proposed free e-tourist visas for visitors from ASEAN member countries. Visitors would still need to apply through India's e-visa portal; only the fee would go.
India already offers a free 30-day e-tourist visa to Thai nationals and announced one for Filipinos in 2025.

sections.title: The rest of the package
paras: The visa offer was one of nine ideas, including a maritime cooperation plan, nuclear energy exchanges, youth programmes and a joint cyber-forensics training programme. ASEAN countries are among India's fastest-growing tourism and trade partners.

facts: E-visa fee waiver proposed, not visa-free entry

stories.head: Sensex falls 500 points to 82,032 and Nifty slips to 25,228 as profit-taking hits metal and consumer durables stocks
stories.dek: Both indices lost about 0.6% after two days of gains, and mid-caps fell harder.

sections.title: The day
paras: The Sensex closed at 82,031.81 on Wednesday, down 500.38 points or 0.61%. The Nifty 50 ended at 25,227.95, down 159.45 points or 0.63%, snapping a two-day winning streak.
Thirteen of 16 major sector indices fell, led by consumer durables and metals. The Nifty Midcap 100 lost 1.22%.

sections.title: What to watch
paras: Analysts called it profit-taking after a strong November run. Big IPOs are open this week, including Coal India's Mahanadi Coalfields from today, and global cues from Anthropic's Nasdaq debut and the Gulf tensions will matter.

stories.head: Bengaluru's Humyn Labs raises $47 million to record everyday human work for training robots
stories.dek: Started this year by ex-Nazara CEO Manish Agarwal and Ishank Gupta, it says it already has over $50 million in annual revenue.

sections.title: The round
paras: Humyn Labs raised $26 million in equity led by Accel, with Prosus Ventures, Bajaj Finance's Finserv Intelligence and Jump Trading among others, plus $21 million in venture debt led by Lighthouse Canton and Trifecta Capital.

sections.title: What it does
paras: The startup films people doing everyday tasks in factories, warehouses, farms and homes, cleans up that data and sells it to AI labs and robotics companies that need real-world examples to train robots. It runs data collection in more than 20 countries and claims over $50 million in annualised revenue within six months.
It will expand in Brazil, South Korea and India, and set up teams in San Francisco, London and Seoul.

stories.head: Israel's parliament elects Matan Kahana as speaker by 66–52, a setback for Netanyahu as rival Gadi Eisenkot tries to form a government
stories.dek: Control of the speaker's chair gives the opposition a say over the parliamentary agenda.

sections.title: The vote
paras: The Knesset chose Matan Kahana of Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party as speaker on 17 November, defeating Likud's Ofir Katz, Netanyahu's pick. Arab-led parties backed Kahana; the two ultra-Orthodox parties did not.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: After last month's inconclusive election, President Isaac Herzog gave Eisenkot 28 days from 8 November to build a coalition. The speaker controls what comes up for votes, which could help lawmakers who want to undo some of Netanyahu's laws. But forming a government remains a much harder task.

stories.head: Palo Alto Networks buys AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5 billion in stock
stories.dek: Applied Compute helps companies train and run their own AI models; the cybersecurity giant wants security built in from the start.

sections.title: The deal
paras: Palo Alto Networks said in a filing that it will buy Applied Compute in an all-stock deal valued at $4.5 billion. It expects to close in its fiscal third quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory approval.
Applied Compute co-founder and CEO Yash Patil said the startup was built to make it easy for any company to train, serve and improve its own AI models.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Big security companies are buying AI firms as businesses roll out AI agents that need guarding. Palo Alto bought observability firm Chronosphere for $3.35 billion a year ago.

facts: Expected close: Palo Alto's fiscal Q3 2027

stories.head: Ola Electric hands scooter sales to dealers, targeting 450 stores by December and over 700 by March 2027
stories.dek: The company stopped taking orders at its own showrooms on 1 November, calling the shift a 'reset' to fix slow service.
stat: Ola Electric's Q2 FY27 revenue fall

sections.title: The switch
paras: Ola Electric has moved from selling scooters directly to a dealer model. It had 255 dealers running 319 stores as of 8 November, and most company-run outlets will close by December.
It aims for 450 dealer stores by December 2026 and more than 700 by March 2027.

sections.title: Why now
paras: Ola says dealers will fix long-running complaints about service delays and paperwork. The move follows a weak quarter: revenue fell 39% to ₹421 crore in July–September. Its auto business borrowings fell to ₹337 crore by September 2026 from ₹2,422 crore in late 2024.

stories.head: Ribbit Capital sells ₹1,905 crore of Groww shares at ₹219 each; its total take from Groww reaches about ₹7,871 crore
stories.dek: Kotak MF, BlackRock, Fidelity, Morgan Stanley and Norges Bank were among the buyers of the roughly 1.4% stake.

sections.title: The deal
paras: Two Ribbit Capital entities sold about 8.7 crore shares of Groww's parent, Billionbrains Garage Ventures, at ₹219 each in NSE block deals on 17 November. That is roughly a 1.4% stake.
Buyers included Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, BlackRock, Societe Generale, Fidelity, BNP Paribas, Morgan Stanley, HDFC Life and Norges Bank.

sections.title: The bigger picture
paras: Ribbit, one of Groww's earliest backers, has now made about ₹7,871 crore from the IPO and three later sales. Early investors selling after a listing is normal; big funds stepping in shows demand for the stock.

stories.credit: Groww app / via Indian Startup News

stories.head: Women's Asian Champions Trophy starts in Bhopal tonight: defending champions India face Malaysia at 7 pm, with free entry
stories.dek: It is India's first tournament since winning gold at the Asian Games in Japan last month.

sections.title: The tournament
paras: Six teams, India, Japan, China, Malaysia, Thailand and South Korea, play at Bhopal's new hockey stadium at the International Sports Complex in Nathu Barkheda from 19 to 28 November. The bronze medal match and final are on 28 November, with rest days on 20, 23 and 26 November.
Hockey India has made entry free for all matches.

sections.title: India's challenge
paras: India won the last edition in Rajgir in 2024 and arrive as Asian Games champions. They open against Malaysia tonight after the opening ceremony.

stories.head: Ramayana: Part 1 reaches ₹844 crore net in India in 14 days, adding ₹23.2 crore on its second Wednesday
stories.dek: Worldwide earnings are now around ₹1,500 crore, according to trade trackers.

sections.title: The numbers
paras: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash's Ramayana: Part 1 earned about ₹23.2 crore net on day 14, down about 19% from day 13, taking its India net total to ₹844.4 crore, according to Sacnilk. Overseas gross is about ₹510 crore.

DNA India reports the worldwide gross has crossed ₹1,500 crore; other estimates put it just under. Either way, it is one of the biggest Indian releases ever and is still adding ₹20 crore-plus on weekdays.

stories.head: Microsoft Ignite: Copilot gets 'Autopilot' agents that keep working on recurring tasks without a prompt at every step
stories.dek: Microsoft also made Copilot Home and Office in Copilot generally available, and will give AI agents their own IDs in Entra.

sections.title: The big announcements
paras: At Ignite in San Francisco on 17 November, Microsoft introduced Autopilot, a long-running agent that handles recurring work and moves projects forward on its own. Copilot Workspaces, a shared space for teams and their agents, is in Microsoft's Frontier early-access programme.
Copilot Home and Office in Copilot became generally available on day one.

sections.title: Keeping agents in check
paras: Microsoft Entra will assign an 'Agent ID' to agents, starting with GitHub Copilot CLI, Claude Code and Autopilot, so their actions can be told apart from human ones. Windows 365 for Agents, a computer-use tool, comes to preview in the Copilot harness in December.

facts: Copilot Home, Office in Copilot: generally available

stories.head: Ethiopia and Eritrea mass troops along their border, raising fears of a new war; fighting reported near Badme
stories.dek: Conflict monitors say Ethiopian forces pushed Tigrayan rebels toward the border; Eritrea denies sending troops into Ethiopia.

sections.title: What's happening
paras: Conflict monitors and people linked to militias in Tigray told Reuters that both countries have gathered forces along the border. Monitoring group ACLED says shelling and fighting broke out near Badme on 9 November, and that on 12 November Ethiopian drones targeted suspected Eritrean positions while Eritrean artillery fired toward Ethiopian lines.
Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of helping Tigrayan rebels, which Eritrea denies.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: The two neighbours fought a border war in 1998–2000 and made peace in 2018. Analysts warn that renewed fighting between Ethiopia's army and Tigray's rebels could drag Eritrea into a direct conflict.

stories.head: This week: Jackie Shroff's Kaali Kheti in theatres, Dhindora 2 on Netflix and Campus Diaries 2 on Prime Video, all on 20 November
stories.dek: Plus Perfect Liars on Prime Video and Anbil Avan on SonyLIV.

sections.title: In theatres
paras: Kaali Kheti, starring Jackie Shroff and Sharad Kelkar, releases on Friday, 20 November. Its makers promoted it with an all black-and-white trailer.

sections.title: Streaming on 20 November
paras: Dhindora Season 2 arrives on Netflix, while Prime Video has Campus Diaries Season 2 and Perfect Liars. SonyLIV has the Tamil title Anbil Avan. Dates sometimes shift, so check the app before you plan a watch.

stories.head: Antarctic blue whales have grown from about 418 to 4,018 since illegal whaling ended in 1973
stories.dek: A new University of Washington-led study shows the planet's largest animals are slowly coming back, though they remain critically endangered.

sections.title: The comeback
paras: Researchers led by Zoe Rand of the University of Washington combined old whaling catch records, photo-identification of individual whales and decades of ship surveys across the Southern Ocean. They estimate the population grew from about 418 animals in 1973 to 4,018, an average of about 4.5% a year.
Killing Antarctic blue whales was banned in 1964, but illegal hunting continued until 1973.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Blue whales breed slowly, with a calf about every three years, so this recovery took decades. They are 'ecosystem engineers': their feeding, waste and even their bodies after death feed thousands of other species. The population is still a small fraction of its pre-whaling size.

stories.head: A brain-only CAR-T therapy from UCSF wiped out a deadly childhood brain cancer in every mouse tested; human trials could start in April 2027
stories.dek: The therapy targets diffuse midline glioma, a tumour that kills nearly all children within a year of diagnosis.
stat: of treated mice cleared of the tumour

sections.title: The breakthrough
paras: Scientists at the University of California, San Francisco engineered immune cells, called B-SYNC CAR-T, that switch on only inside the brain. Delivered directly into the brain, they eliminated diffuse midline glioma in every mouse tested across two models, while standard CAR-T cells could not control the tumours. The results are in Science Translational Medicine.
Seven weeks later, every treated mouse rejected a fresh dose of tumour cells, and the cells were still working more than 70 days on.

sections.title: What's next
paras: UCSF is preparing a first human trial, possibly from April 2027, co-led by Dr Sabine Mueller. It has not yet been tested in people, but for a cancer with almost no treatment options, it is real hope.

stories.head: Two women turn the paddy straw farmers burn into fuel pellets, building a ₹7–8 crore-a-year business in Sirsa
stories.dek: Sanjana and Sonika's company buys stubble that would otherwise be set on fire and sells pellets to power plants.

sections.title: From smoke to fuel
paras: Sanjana from Ghoranwali village in Haryana's Sirsa district and Sonika from Bhadra in Rajasthan started SSAR Biomass Green in 2024. They invested about ₹2.5 crore with help from the government's Agriculture Infrastructure Fund to set up a unit in Ghoranwali.
The plant turns leftover paddy straw, or parali, into compact biofuel pellets sold to power plants. It handles about 1 to 1.5 lakh quintals of straw a year.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Burning stubble is a big cause of north India's winter smog. By paying for straw, the business gives farmers a reason not to burn it, creates work for local baler operators, and employs more than 20 people. Turnover is now ₹7–8 crore a year.

facts: 1–1.5 lakh quintals of straw a year

stories.head: Algeria flies Kansas families who cheered its World Cup team to Algiers for a thank-you trip of a lifetime
stories.dek: When Algeria based itself in Lawrence, Kansas, for the 2026 World Cup, the town adopted the team. Algeria has now returned the favour.

sections.title: A friendship from football
paras: During the 2026 World Cup, Algeria's team chose Lawrence, Kansas, as its base. Locals and hundreds of Algerian fans from across North America filled the town, and a resident's thank-you video to Algeria got tens of millions of views.

sections.title: The return trip
paras: This month, at the Algerian president's invitation, Lawrence Mayor Brad Finkeldei, local fans, and police officers who guarded the team's training flew to Algeria. They were greeted with flowers at 4:30 am, toured the Roman ruins of Tipaza, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and watched Algeria beat Togo 1-0 in an Africa Cup of Nations qualifier.

stories.head: The SS United States, once the world's fastest ocean liner, is sunk off Florida to become the world's largest artificial reef
stories.dek: The 1952 record-breaker now rests about 180 feet down off Destin, where it will shelter fish and draw divers.
stat: what Okaloosa County paid for the ship

sections.title: A new life underwater
paras: The SS United States was sunk on 11 November about 22–25 miles off Destin, Florida, after months of cleaning to remove harmful materials. It is now the world's largest artificial reef, beating the aircraft carrier USS Oriskany, sunk off Pensacola in 2006.
Okaloosa County bought the liner in 2024 for $1 million; the reef project is budgeted at $13.5 million.

sections.title: A record-holder
paras: In 1952 the ship crossed the Atlantic in 3 days, 10 hours and 40 minutes, still the fastest by a passenger liner. Instead of being scrapped, it will now support corals, fish and a dive-tourism economy.

stories.head: US homelessness falls about 6% in a year, the biggest single-year drop since 2007
stories.dek: Official and independent counts both show tens of thousands fewer people without a home, the second yearly fall in a row.

sections.title: The numbers
paras: The National Alliance to End Homelessness estimates about 693,000 people were homeless on a single night in 2026, roughly 49,000 fewer than a year before, a 6.7% fall. HUD's own 2026 count found 698,425 people, a 6.3% drop.
Sheltered homelessness fell 7.6% and homelessness among veterans fell nearly 8%, the Alliance said.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: It is the second straight yearly decline and the biggest since 2007. Numbers are still above pre-Covid levels, and chronic homelessness rose about 1%, but advocates credit local housing programmes and front-line workers for the progress.

facts: Second yearly fall in a row

stories.head: Siblings in China build a 430-step 'sky ladder' up a mountain so their 86-year-old mother can visit her old home
stories.dek: The family spent three months hauling stones and cement, and the new path now helps hikers and herb gatherers too.

sections.title: A gift for Mum
paras: Huang Zhulian, 58, and her siblings in Zhejiang province built the stairway for their mother, Mrs Chen, who grew up on the mountain and never settled into town life. The old path she used each April for the Qingming festival had become overgrown and full of snakes.
Brothers and cousins carried stones and mixed cement, other relatives cooked and cleared rubble, and a grandson used a heavy-lift drone to move stones. Some sections are fixed to a sheer cliff.

sections.title: Worth it
paras: Work ran from August to October. Mrs Chen put in 50,000 yuan (about $7,500) from her savings. Huang says she lost weight, got tanned and lost hair, but has no regrets.
